land.text: the Malwa-plateau part of the Ahar country; 'preceded by the Kayatha, Ahar-Banas, and Savalda cultures'

predecessors.note: Kayatha and Savalda have no dossier. The handover year is bridging.

land.text: 'succeeded by the Jorwe culture and the Black and red ware culture'; the Jorwe page: 'preceded by the Malwa culture' and 'also reached north into the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh'

successors.note: The Maharashtra sites pass to Jorwe in -1400, the Malwa plateau in -1300.

correction.text: 'existed in the Malwa region of Central India and parts of Maharashtra in the Deccan Peninsula': the Malwa plateau (Navdatoli near Maheshwar, Eran, Nagda, Vidisha, Mandsaur, Kayatha) and the Maharashtra sites Daimabad (Ahmednagar) and Inamgaon (Pune), drawn as 60 km discs on Ahmednagar and Pune; the Ahar-Banas country is left to the Ahar-Banas dossier until -1600

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). 'It is mainly dated to c. 1600 - c. 1300 BCE'; calibrated radiocarbon dates 'have suggested that the beginning of this culture may be as early as c. 2000-1750 BCE'. The page gives no area; the shape resolves to about 178,000 km2 (the plateau 154,500 plus the Maharashtra discs 23,500).

correction.text: 'existed in the Malwa region of Central India and parts of Maharashtra in the Deccan Peninsula': the Malwa plateau (Navdatoli near Maheshwar, Eran, Nagda, Vidisha, Mandsaur, Kayatha) and the Maharashtra sites Daimabad (Ahmednagar) and Inamgaon (Pune), drawn as 60 km discs on Ahmednagar and Pune; the Ahar-Banas country is left to the Ahar-Banas dossier until -1600

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Maharashtra sites (Daimabad, Inamgaon) are also Jorwe sites, whose early phase the Jorwe page dates 'c. 1400-1000 BCE'; the Malwa plateau alone remains to -1300.

region.text: 'existed in the Malwa region of Central India and parts of Maharashtra in the Deccan Peninsula': the Malwa plateau (Navdatoli near Maheshwar, Eran, Nagda, Vidisha, Mandsaur, Kayatha) and the Maharashtra sites Daimabad (Ahmednagar) and Inamgaon (Pune), drawn as 60 km discs on Ahmednagar and Pune; the Ahar-Banas country is left to the Ahar-Banas dossier until -1600

ledger.note: c. 1600 BCE: the Malwa Chalcolithic culture stands on the Malwa plateau and in the north Deccan. 'It is mainly dated to c. 1600 - c. 1300 BCE' (the beginning 'may be as early as c. 2000-1750 BCE'); 'existed in the Malwa region of Central India and parts of Maharashtra in the Deccan Peninsula'. The year is the page's 'mainly' date; the country is the page's region and sites.

region.text: the Malwa-plateau part of the Ahar country

ledger.note: c. 1600 BCE: the Malwa culture takes over the Malwa-plateau sites of the Ahar-Banas culture (Mandsaur, Kayatha). 'preceded by the Kayatha, Ahar-Banas, and Savalda cultures'; no page dates the handover.

region.text: Daimabad (Ahmednagar) and Inamgaon (Pune), sites of both pages

ledger.note: c. 1400 BCE: the Maharashtra sites pass to the Jorwe culture. The Jorwe page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorwe_culture) dates its early phase 'c. 1400-1000 BCE' and names Daimabad and Inamgaon among its sites; the Malwa page lists the same two among its own. Both pages name the sites; neither dates the handover.

c. 1300 BCE: the Malwa culture gives way to the Jorwe culture. 'It is mainly dated to c. 1600 - c. 1300 BCE', 'succeeded by the Jorwe culture and the Black and red ware culture'. The page gives no phases and no account of the end.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture known from eight named sites; the page names no rivers or districts.

sources.title: Malwa culture
sources.note: Dates 1600-1300 (maybe from 2000-1750), region 'Malwa region of Central India and parts of Maharashtra', eight sites, preceded by Kayatha, Ahar-Banas and Savalda, succeeded by Jorwe and Black and red ware.

sources.title: Jorwe culture
sources.note: Used for the Maharashtra handover: Jorwe early phase c. 1400-1000, Daimabad and Inamgaon as Jorwe sites, preceded by the Malwa culture.

notes: Type culture; no Cliopatria row; no area on the page. The Malwa region of the gazetteer (about 155,000 km2, 74.0-78.5E 22.0-25.15N) is the whole plateau, much larger than eight sites prove; the page names no rivers or districts, so a gap-filler may prefer a smaller shape. Maharashtra: the two discs are my reading of 'parts of Maharashtra in the Deccan Peninsula' from the named sites Daimabad and Inamgaon (Ahmednagar and Pune districts, not gazetteer places). The pairing with Jorwe (Maharashtra to Jorwe in -1400, the plateau in -1300) rests on the two pages' date ranges (Malwa 1600-1300, Jorwe from 1400), not on a dated handover. The Harappan civilisation is not mentioned on the page; the Savalda culture and the Kayatha culture have no dossier.
